title: Affinity shards + spillover windows for multi-zone dedicated pools with residency assertions
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Summary:
Implement an affinity-sharding model with controlled spillover windows for multi-zone dedicated GPU pools to satisfy per-customer data residency constraints while preserving throughput guarantees and safe autoscaling behavior.

Problem:
- Customers reserve Dedicated capacity per region but increasingly require soft affinity to particular zones for performance or legal reasons. Current placement is either strict zone-lock (poor utilization) or fully permissive (violates residency assertions).
- Autoscaler and capacity spillover today have no notion of timed windows or residency-preserving ordering, leading to noisy failovers and sudden cross-zone migrations that break compliance and client expectations.

Goals:
- Provide a first-class "affinity shards" primitive: a set of zone preference tags and an ordered spillover policy (primary -> secondary -> tertiary) with configurable spillover windows.
- Ensure throughput guarantees: honor reserved throughput within the primary affinity when capacity available; when scaled across zones, surface guarantees and degraded SLOs to customers.
- Integrate policies with autoscaler so scale-up/down decisions respect spillover ordering and avoid oscillation.
- Expose residency assertions in API/console so customers can opt for strict or soft residency and see expected impact on latency/cost.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does NOT implement cross-region data-migration tooling or stateful KV replication.
- Does not change billing model (reserved vs on-demand) — only placement semantics.

Design proposal (high level):
1) Affinity shards metadata
   - Each Dedicated pool gets an optional affinity_shards array of tags: ["zone-a-primary","zone-b-secondary"].
   - A residency_mode: {"STRICT","PREFERENTIAL","BEST_EFFORT"} (api values).
2) Spillover windows
   - A time-bound ordering: when primary zone utilization > threshold for sustained period (configurable), the orchestrator opens a spillover window to the next zone for a configured duration (default 15m).
   - During the window, placement prefers existing inflight KV cache locality and tries to co-locate for minimal cold-start.
3) Throughput guarantees and degraded SLOs
   - Controller tracks per-pool reserved tokens/sec. When spillover is active, we calculate expected per-zone latency uplift and expose a per-pool "degraded_throughput" estimate to the Console and API.
4) Autoscaler/Orchestrator integration
   - Autoscaler will use a weighted objective: prefer scaling in-zone first, only open spillover when utilization cannot be satisfied in any single zone without violating reserved throughput.
   - Backoff and hysteresis added to avoid cascade migrations.
5) Residency assertions enforcement
   - For STRICT: placement forbidden outside zone(s) in shard; requests return 429 or queued with clear error and SLA note.
   - For PREFERENTIAL: allow spillover windows with configured max_duration per day; log policy breaches and alert customers.

API and Console changes:
- New fields in pool API: affinity_shards (list), residency_mode, spillover_policy {threshold_pct, window_seconds, max_daily_spill_seconds}.
- Console: pool details view with visualization of active spillover and expected degraded throughput.
- Alerting: automatic alert to customer and Redwood SRE when STRICT policy is violated.

Operational concerns and trade-offs:
- Benefit: higher utilization and predictable behavior versus strict zone-lock which wastes reserved capacity.
- Risk: increased cross-zone traffic could add egress and KV cold-cache penalties, affecting latency. We mitigate by: (a) encouraging customers to pin hot-state where needed, (b) providing degraded throughput estimates, (c) limiting daily spill durations for PREFERENTIAL.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Unit + integration tests for placement logic and spillover timers.
- Chaos test: simulate zone degradation and verify ordered spillover and autoscaler hysteresis.
- Pilot: opt-in for a subset of Dedicated customers (5 customers) for a 4-week pilot with SRE-run escalations.
- Gradual rollout: Feature-flag behind runtime-2 with telemetry gating for 7 days then GA.

Metrics to monitor:
- per-pool spillover_open_rate, spillover_duration_seconds, frequency_of_strict_violations, degraded_throughput_ratio, autoscaler_actions_per_minute, cross_zone_egress_bytes.

Backward compatibility:
- Default residency_mode = PREFERENTIAL with conservative defaults (threshold 85%, window 900s). Existing pools unchanged until explicitly migrated.

Docs & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/d/dedicated/affinity-shards-spillover
- UX mockups: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/affinity-spillover-console.png
- Draft API PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2048

Acceptance criteria:
- Affinity shards metadata accepted by API and persisted in pool objects.
- Orchestrator honors spillover ordering and timers under controlled traffic tests.
- Autoscaler respects residency_mode and avoids >2 cross-zone migrations per hour for a pool under steady load.
- Console shows active spillover and degraded throughput estimate for pilot customers.
